senses.gloss: m. pl. (used as sing.), constr. כּוּרְסֵי, כָּרְסֵא (כרס; cmp. כַּר) divan, upholstered chair, throne.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Kings 10:19">Targ. I Kings X, 19</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 17:16">Targ. Ex. XVII, 16</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Chullin 59b">Ḥull. 59ᵇ</cite> [read:] <he>נפל מִכּוּרְסַיֵּיה וכ׳</he> he fell from his throne to the ground.

<cite ref="Yevamot 118b:17">Yeb. 118ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Ketubot 75a:5">Keth. 75ᵃ</cite> <he>דשומשנא גברא כּוּרְסְיָהּ … רמי לה</he> if her husband be (as small as) an ant, put up her seat among the women of nobility, i.e. a woman feels elevated by marriage.
<cite ref="Yevamot 83b:6">Yeb. 83ᵇ</cite> <he>אותבוה אבי כורסי׳</he> they put him on an operator’s chair.

<cite ref="Yevamot 110a:5">Ib. 110ᵃ</cite> <he>אותבוה אבי כ׳ ואהדרוה</he> Ar. (ed. omit <he>ואהדרוה</he>) they put her on a bridal chair (v. <cite ref="A02817"><he>אַפִּרְיוֹן</he></cite>) and carried her around in procession.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 27">Lev. R. s. 27</cite> <he>תחות כ׳ דאמהון</he> under their mothers’ chair (of delivery); <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 2:4">Midr. Till. to Ps. II</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 165:1">Yalk. Ex. 165</cite>; Yalk. Esth. 1055 (only <he>תחות כורסי</he>).
Gitt. 35ᵃ הפכוה לכוּרְסְיֵה (fem.) turn his judicial chair over; הפכוה לכ׳ ותרצוה (Rashi: הפכו) they turned his chair over and set it up again; a. fr.—Pl. כּוּרְסָוָון, כָּרְסָוָן, כּוּרְסְוָתָא.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 122:5">Targ. Ps. CXXII, 5</cite>.—
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 3:9:1">Koh. R. to III, 9</cite> <he>אית דאייתי כ׳</he> some brought divans (for the banquet).
Ib. to I, 8 (in Hebr. Dict.) יעשו כ׳ לרבים (sub. בתי) let them be made into privies for the public.
